h: Ironbridge, the Wrekin and a Bounce in Between
p: Telford is a newer town wrapped around a very old landscape, and that mix makes it a great base for a family weekend. Because this branch sits right in the shopping centre, you can easily slot a session in between the bigger days out the area is famous for, rather than making a special trip just for the trampolines.

The Ironbridge Gorge is the obvious headline. The world's first major iron bridge still spans the Severn there, and the Gorge museums spread out around it. Blists Hill Victorian Town is the one most kids love, with its cobbled street, old shops and costumed characters, while Enginuity lets them push, pull and build their way through hands-on engineering challenges. Both are a few miles from the town centre.

If you'd rather be outdoors, the Wrekin is the hill you can see from all over Shropshire. The climb is steady rather than brutal and the views from the top are cracking on a clear day, though small legs may need a few rest stops on the way up. Closer to the centre, the Southwater area beside the shopping centre has restaurants and places for a sit-down once everyone's worn out.

A sensible way to plan it is to treat the trampolines as the reward. Do your sightseeing in the morning while the kids are still willing, then let them loose in the afternoon. Wear stretchy clothes, keep pockets empty, and take a drink in with you, because a short session works up a proper thirst.

Book ahead if you're visiting in the school holidays, when Telford's attractions and the shopping centre both get busier. And if you're staying over, the Ironbridge museums often work out better value with a pass that covers several sites, so it's worth checking before you buy tickets one by one.
